limitations: A single run over a small dataset is indicative, not statistical.
Actual model outputs are nondeterministic; repeated live runs can differ.

Keyword-based figures are heuristic proxies, not measures of factual correctness: paraphrases cause false negatives, keywords inside wrong or negated statements cause false positives, and forbidden lists are not exhaustive.
Similarity-score distributions are descriptive only; no threshold is derived or applied.
Database verification checks chunk identity, metadata and content against the repository corpus; it does not establish which model computed the stored embedding vectors.
Provider token usage is reported only for completed responses; usage of failed, timed-out or retried attempts is unknown and may still be billed.
The worst-case output-token bound is not a total cost bound: input tokens and provider pricing are not included.

questions.answer: An HTTP 401 from the registry's /v2/ endpoint is normal for a registry that requires authentication and shows that the registry is reachable. [3]

A Linux filesystem can run out of inodes, which limit the number of files it can hold, while disk blocks may still be available. [2]
Inode exhaustion can be checked with the df -i command, which shows 100% IUse% when inodes are full, even though df -h shows free space. [4]

The root cause was an unbounded log archive on the worker node. [4]
A batch job wrote logs to /var/log/app-archive on the node, and no log rotation or retention rule existed for that path. [4]
Over several months the archive filled the shared /var filesystem, so the container runtime could not write the layers of the new image. [4]

The sources do not state a specific value. The completed follow-up set the keep-alive and headers timeouts explicitly in the storefront server code, with a comment linking them to the load balancer idle timeout. [3]

The new 5.8.0 release increased the memory needed at startup beyond the container limit of 1Gi, so the kernel killed the container with OOMKilled. [4]
After the kernel killed the container, the kubelet restarted it repeatedly, which led to CrashLoopBackOff with growing restart delays. [4]
The configuration value was changed to 250ms instead of 250, a format the application could not parse. [2]

INC-2025-002 was caused by a keep-alive timeout mismatch on the storefront service. [1]
INC-2025-003 was caused by search-api pods being OOMKilled and then stuck in CrashLoopBackOff. [3]
The service was restored by reverting the invalid ConfigMap change, which is marked as completed in the incident's action items. [5]
